newsitem.title: GERMANY: China Eastern ups ex-Germany air cargo rates 5pct.
newsitem.headline: China Eastern ups ex-Germany air cargo rates 5pct.

text.p: China Eastern Airlines said it has raised its ex-Germany air cargo rates by five percent from the beginning of this month.
Jie Xu, the carrier's Germany cargo sales manager, said strong demand for freight space and limited market capacity justified the higher prices.
"Shipments are coming in regularly and with a rates increase, we can make more profits," he told Reuters in an interview.
China Eastern flies twice-weekly Munich-Shanghai flights, with a Beijing stopover, with Airbus A340 aircraft that can uplift a maximum nine tonnes of cargo.
Xu noted that Lufthansa Cargo and Swissair had also recently raised ex-Germany rates to China by at least five percent.

The Shanghai-based carrier had higher rates than the market average of 3.30 marks a kg for a 100kg shipment shown in the latest Reuters market survey but lower than top market rates of about 3.80 marks, he noted.
Air cargo market rates to China had fallen since last summer with heavy competition for larger shipments, Xu added.
